source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. CPU Common Options → SMU and PSP Debug Mode: Disabled e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Uncorrectable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --smupsp --socket 0 --errormode 1 --enablemcapolling 0 --errorindex 0 --errortype 1 5.1 The system will reset immediately. 5.2 When system boot into operating system again, check dmesg log. 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- MP1 (SMU) Uncorrectable Error: inject the MP1 SMU MP1 (SMU) Uncorrectable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'smu|mp1|mp5|mpio|firmware.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __MP1_SMU_MP1_(SMU)_Uncorrectable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.
